text:
sam: Heads-up — seeing steady memory growth on long streaming chats when tool loops are enabled. Investigating whether KV compaction signals aren't firing under continuous append.

lina: how big is the growth? percentage or absolute?

sam: ~120-180MB/hour on a 32GB worker for sessions that run >2h and repeatedly call tool plugins. Not an immediate OOM but cumulative across many sessions is worrying.

prateek: do you have a profile? heap, malloc traces, or pprof?

sam: attached a short heap sample from staging run (snip):
```
heap profile: top 10 objects by alloc size
1  kv_cache::PageChain  78MB  (retained)
2  kv_cache::SlotMap    36MB
3  std::string (prompts) 18MB
4  grpc::CallState      10MB
alloc_count increased steadily when tool loop iteration > 300
```

jules: that PageChain number jumps out. Could be threads holding references so compactor can't free. Any long-lived refs in tool loop?

sam: tool loop keeps handles to partial outputs and occasionally pins a reference for the external tool bridge. We thought weak refs would allow eviction but maybe not.

kevin: quick check: are we skipping compaction if page churn is below threshold? there was a recent change to avoid compaction noise that gates on page_fault_rate < 0.0005.

prateek: iirc we also changed kernel selection path to favor a faster small-kernel that avoids scanning full page lists to keep latency stable. That could mean compaction bookkeeping isn't run.

lina: matt from infra mentioned a perf regression PR ~2 weeks ago touching batch heuristics and `should_schedule_compaction()` -> might be related.

sam: repro steps i used: start long streaming chat with a tool loop that calls `fetch_context()` every 10 messages, keep streaming KV writes, run for ~3h. Use the attached debug flags: `--kv-debug=pages,compaction` and `--kv-evict-threshold=0.6`.

prateek: can you paste the debug trace lines around compaction decisions?

sam: here's an excerpt: \n```
[00:42:10] kv: inserting page id=0x7f3a size=8192
[00:42:11] kv: page_faults=2 active_pages=482 free_pages=22
[00:42:12] kv: compaction_skipped: low_fault_rate (0.0003) kernel=fast-no-scan
[01:10:05] kv: inserting page id=0x7f4b size=8192
[01:10:06] kv: page_faults=3 active_pages=510 free_pages=18
[01:10:07] kv: compaction_skipped: low_fault_rate (0.00025) kernel=fast-no-scan
```\n
jules: that shows compaction being skipped because of the low fault rate check. But active_pages keeps rising. The heuristic assumes fault rate correlates with fragmentation — clearly false for long streaming tool loops.

kevin: proposal: add an elastic window check on active_pages delta over time and trigger compaction if growth > X pages within Y seconds, regardless of fault rate. Also temporarily force a full-scan compaction on kernel-switch if kernel=oscan->fast-no-scan.

prateek: agree. Also verify weak_ref behavior in tool-bridge — if we hold shared_ptr in the python bridge for partial outputs, that prevents page release. I'll audit the bridge code.

lina: for short-term mitigation: bump `--kv-evict-threshold` lower on staging/dedicated pools for streaming workloads and flip on a forced hourly compact cron.

sam: i started a canary with hourly compaction cron + the windowed growth check enabled on staging. early signs: memory plateaued after 30m instead of continuing linear climb.

prateek: can you open a small PR with the patch to `should_schedule_compaction()` + unit tests simulating long session churn? Keep the default off behind a feature flag.

sam: will do. PR will include a test harness that simulates streaming-toolloop workload and asserts compaction triggers when active_pages delta > 64 in 5 minutes.

jules: also add instrumentation: expose `active_pages_delta` and `compaction_skipped_reason` to the console dashboard so we can correlate with tenant workloads.

kevin: after PR we should run a 24h soak against the long-context benchmark to ensure no perf regression from extra compaction metadata checks. include kernel-switch path coverage.

lina: sounds good. Next steps: sam PR + staging soak; prateek audit bridge; jules dashboard metrics; kevin soak. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: compact-cron toggle ON on staging at 2026-03-19T09:12:00Z
